issues_detected.description: The processing documentation does not describe the distributed artifacts. All four preprocessing_strategies entries and the single labeling_strategies entry carry source_caveats stating that they are steps of the MuSIC pipeline whose cell-map outputs are 'not included in this release', one of them adding explicitly that 'this step was not applied to the artifacts distributed here'. The first cleaning_strategies entry is caveated the same way. What remains applicable to the released archives is one vague sentence ('Data generated by the acquisition modules undergo quality control before release') plus FAIRSCAPE RO-Crate packaging. Three of the five file_collections are typed collection_type: processed_data (AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq), so the released data were processed, yet no mass-spectrometry search or quantification step, no single-cell alignment or counting step, and no image-processing step is described for them.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add preprocessing_strategies and cleaning_strategies entries that describe the pipeline actually applied to the released AP-MS, SEC-MS and perturb-seq archives (search engine and FDR thresholds, elution-profile processing, read alignment and guide assignment, image acquisition-to-archive processing), and keep the MuSIC pipeline steps clearly separated as downstream methodology.

issues_detected.description: No software is named in a producing or transforming role for the released data. The software the record does name falls outside that role: FAIRSCAPE client/framework performs RO-Crate packaging, provenance-metadata generation and input validation (packaging/metadata production and validation roles); the University of Virginia Dataverse is the hosting and serving platform; the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit is a capture reagent used at acquisition; and node2vec, the Human Protein Atlas embedding model, the contrastive co-embedding and community-detection steps, the Cell Mapping Toolkit (github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline) and the Integrative Modeling Platform all belong to pipelines the record itself states produced outputs that are not in this release, or that consume the release downstream. No used_software is attached to any property, and machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are absent. No version number is given for any named software.
issues_detected.recommendation: Attach used_software to the processing steps that produced the released archives, naming the mass-spectrometry search/quantification software, the single-cell processing software and the image-handling software, each with a version and, where available, a repository or software DOI.

issues_detected.description: No variable-level metadata anywhere in the record. The variables slot is absent, is_tabular is absent, and no subsets block carries is_data_split or is_subpopulation flags. The release distributes AP-MS, SEC-MS and perturb-seq tables that are inherently tabular, but a reuser is given no column names, no units, no identifier scheme and no data dictionary for any of them.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add a variables block with identifiers, types, units and descriptions for the columns of the AP-MS, SEC-MS and perturb-seq tables, and set is_tabular for the tabular collections.

issues_detected.description: The record omits publisher on the stated ground that 'The bundle names no publisher for the release', yet its own citation field prints 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2' in the publisher position of the citation, page resolves to dataverse.lib.virginia.edu, description says the data are 'archived in the University of Virginia Dataverse', and maintainers and retention_limit both name the UVA Dataverse (LibraData) as archival steward. The omission is therefore inconsistent with four other fields of the same record.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate publisher with University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), which the record's own citation, landing page and stewardship fields already assert.

issues_detected.description: No anomalies documentation. The anomalies slot is absent and no substitute covers data-content quality issues: batch effects, failed or non-specific antibodies, discarded images, failed mass-spectrometry runs, low-complexity cells or filtered guides are nowhere discussed. known_limitations covers scope, coverage, embargo and expertise, and missing_data_documentation covers what is absent, but neither documents anomalies within the data that are present.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add an anomalies block recording known quality issues in the released imaging, mass-spectrometry and single-cell data, including any filtering already applied and any residual artifacts users should expect.

issues_detected.description: Deidentification is asserted without a formal method and without a residual-risk assessment. is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false and deidentification_details argue the material is non-identifiable because it derives from commercially available cell lines that 'cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject'. No recognised standard (Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity) is named and no identifiers_removed list is given. The rationale is also not tested against the record's own content: both lines are donor-derived and named, the record states MDA-MB-468 has public whole-genome sequencing data available, and the release distributes single-cell transcriptomic data, so genotype-based linkage is a risk the record asserts away rather than assesses.
issues_detected.recommendation: State the basis of the de-identification determination explicitly (donor-derived immortalised line distributed under existing repository terms) and add a short residual-risk note addressing genotype-based linkage from the released sequence-derived data.

issues_detected.description: Data formats are described only at the container level. distribution_formats gives 'ZIP archives containing RO-Crate packaged data files and metadata' with media_type application/zip, and conforms_to names JSON-LD, RDF-XML and JSON-Schema for the metadata and provenance layer, but no format is stated for the payload: the image files inside the three immunofluorescence archives, the AP-MS and SEC-MS tables and the perturb-seq matrices. Character encoding is stated nowhere.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add per-collection format and media_type entries for the archive contents (for example OME-TIFF or PNG for images, TSV or mzTab for mass-spectrometry output, MTX/H5AD for single-cell matrices) and state the character encoding of text files.

issues_detected.description: Release-scope instance counts are largely unstated. instances describes four instance types but reports no counts. The figures in notes (1,374 protein interactions, 53,788 immunofluorescent images, 7,023 proteins, 21.4 TB) are explicitly flagged as project-wide across all quarterly releases rather than for this release, and source_caveats explains, defensibly, why the per-file protein counts from the October 2025 release are not carried over. The only release-scope sample count is the 11,739 genes targeted by the iPSC perturbation atlas. A user therefore cannot say how many images, cells or interactions this release contains.
issues_detected.recommendation: Report release-scope counts per modality (images per condition, cells per perturb-seq archive, baits and interactions per AP-MS archive), or state that the source does not provide them, rather than leaving the reader to infer scope from project-wide totals.

issues_detected.description: Locally minted DOI fragment identifiers are used as identifiers for entities that have no DOI. Three grants carry ids of the form doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#grant-1OT2OD032742-01 and nine creators carry ids of the form doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#creator-axelsson-u. A fragment appended to a registered DOI does not resolve and is not itself registered, so these identifiers are not dereferenceable even though the underlying award numbers they encode are correct and are also written out in the accompanying notes.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record award numbers in a grant-identifier slot rather than as DOI fragments, and leave creator ids empty or use a non-DOI local identifier scheme where no ORCID exists, keeping the names and affiliations in notes as the record already does.

issues_detected.description: No download_url and no errata. The download_url slot is empty; access is conveyed through distribution_formats.access_urls, one of which is the landing page and the other the Dataverse data-access API base https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/, which is a truncated endpoint requiring a file identifier that the record does not supply for any of the ten archives. The errata slot is likewise empty, and there is no consolidated release-level changelog; what changed since the October 2025 release has to be reconstructed from source_caveats.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate download_url with the resolvable landing or access URL, list the Dataverse file identifiers so the API pattern is usable, and add an errata or release-notes entry summarising what changed in the June 2026 release.

issues_detected.description: Two disclosed but unresolved source conditions sit in tension with other assertions. First, the CM4AI portal's 'Released on: June 17, 2025' against the Dataverse publication date of 2026-06-17 is a one-year discrepancy that the record resolves by source ranking without reconciling; the internal dates it does assert (created_on 2025-02-27, issued 2026-06-17, distribution_dates 2026-06-17 and 2026-07-15) are mutually ordered and consistent. Second, notes records that the hosting Dataverse collection 'is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives', which is an availability risk that retention_limit's commitment to 'long term preservation ... supported by committed institutional funds' does not acknowledge.
issues_detected.recommendation: Note in retention_limit that the hosting collection is under review, so that the preservation commitment is read alongside the disclosed risk to it.

issues_detected.description: imputation_protocols is absent and is not documented as unused. missing_data_documentation describes what is missing from the release and why, but does not state whether any imputation was performed on the released mass-spectrometry or single-cell data, where missing values are routine.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add an imputation_protocols entry stating either the imputation method applied to missing quantitative values or that no imputation was performed.

semantic_insights: Element 4 applicability resolves cleanly on evidence outside Element 4. Description and keywords name two cell lines (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J iPSC) and no participants, patients or clinical research; collection_mechanisms describe endogenous tagging, chromatography, antibody staining and CRISPR screens rather than recruitment; direct_collection.is_direct is false with the statement 'Data were not collected from individuals'. The human-subjects condition therefore plainly fails, so sub-elements 3 to 5 are not applicable. Regulatory_restrictions (E2) nonetheless state an applying constraint (clinical or patient-care use requires regulatory oversight and approval) and other_compliance names a Data Governance Committee contact, and both cell lines are donor-derived, so the governance disjunct opens sub-elements 1 and 2, which are scored.

Identifier coherence is strong across registrars. The DOI 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C is well-formed, and the 10.18130 prefix is the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) registrant, matching the dataverse.lib.virginia.edu landing page and the repository named in the citation. Related identifiers are equally plausible: 10.1101 for two bioRxiv preprints, 10.1038 for a Nature paper, four sibling 10.18130/V3/ release DOIs, RRID:CVCL_0419 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3 as Cellosaurus cell-line RRIDs, and well-formed ORCID and ROR identifiers throughout.

All four NIH award numbers match agency pattern. OT2OD032742 parses as activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032742; 1OT2OD032742-01 and 3OT2OD032742-01S2 add valid application-type prefixes and support-year suffixes; 5U54HG012513-02 parses as a type-5 U54 centre award from NHGRI, consistent with its stated grantor 'National Institutes of Health, Bridge2AI Bridge Center'. The unnumbered third funder, the Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia, is correctly recorded without a grant block and with an explicit statement that no identifier is given.

The record practises unusual scope discipline about counts. Notes explicitly separates project-wide cumulative totals from release-scope figures, and observes that the 11,739-gene figure coincides at both scopes while being stated at different ones. Sampling_strategies declines to carry over the 464 and 563 protein counts from earlier releases, giving a concrete reason: the June 2026 image archives report the same file sizes as October 2025 but different MD5 checksums, indicating regeneration. This costs the record coverage but is the correct handling of a source conflict.

The record discloses the limits of its own processing documentation. Rather than presenting the MuSIC pipeline as the provenance of the distributed files, every preprocessing entry carries a caveat that the cell maps are not in this release, one saying outright that the step 'was not applied to the artifacts distributed here'. That candour is what makes the Element 8 gap diagnosable; it does not close the gap, because the processing that did produce the released processed_data archives is still unstated.

Cross-field arithmetic and cross-references check out. The five file_collections file_counts sum to 3+2+2+2+1 = 10, matching total_file_count. The four prior-release DOIs in related_datasets are the same four listed in version_access.versions_available. The ethical_reviews contact_person ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801 resolves to the creators entry for Ravitsky V. Version '2.0' agrees with the citation's 'V2' and with version_access.

Licence semantics are coherent across four fields. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 in license_and_use_terms matches data_use_permission: no_commercial_use, the ShareAlike and no-further-restrictions clauses reappear as prohibited_uses, and the commercial-negotiation route reappears in ip_restrictions with the copyright allocation between the Regents of the University of California and the Board of Trustees of Stanford, the latter specifically for the raw spatial-proteomics images produced in the Lundberg lab.

Explicit false flags carry reasoning rather than boilerplate. sensitive_elements_present: false is accompanied by a statement of what the released content actually consists of and why it is not PHI; involves_human_subjects: false is accompanied by an ethics_review_board narrative explaining that no IRB approval is recorded precisely because no human subjects are involved, with named ethics contacts providing the alternative oversight route. These are documented determinations, not empty negatives.

The three limitation-facing elements reinforce each other. known_limitations (cell maps absent, incomplete panel overlap, embargo, expertise required, iPSC imaging forthcoming), missing_data_documentation (the same absences with causes and a handling strategy) and known_biases (representation and selection bias, the latter with a concrete mitigation) describe the same gaps consistently rather than contradicting one another, and sampling_strategies.why_not_representative reuses the representation-bias wording verbatim.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; raw_data_sources carry RRID:CVCL_0419 (MDA-MB-468) and RRID:CVCL_B5P3 (KOLF2.1J)
sub_elements.quality_note: A single persistent identifier is used consistently as the DOI, the record id and the latest-version pointer, and the four prior releases are identified by sibling DOIs under the same prefix. Cell-line RRIDs additionally identify the source material.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: DOI matches the 10.XXXXX/... pattern; the 10.18130 prefix is the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) registrant and is corroborated by the dataverse.lib.virginia.edu landing page and by the repository named in the citation, so the prefix is plausible rather than merely well-formed. CVCL_ is the Cellosaurus RRID namespace and both cell-line RRIDs are well-formed.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description of roughly 1,600 characters naming the two cell lines, the three MDA-MB-468 treatment conditions, the four KOLF2.1J differentiation states, the four assay modalities (perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS, immunofluorescence), the RO-Crate/FAIRSCAPE packaging, the archive, the scientific objective and the nine collaborating institutions
sub_elements.quality_note: Far beyond the 200-character threshold and substantive throughout: a reader learns what was measured, on what material, under which perturbations, in what packaging and to what end. The title disambiguates the release from its siblings by date and status.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Description content matches the claimed dataset type: every modality it names reappears in instances, file_collections and acquisition_methods, and the cell lines it names reappear in raw_data_sources with RRIDs. No overclaiming: the description does not assert computed cell maps, which known_limitations confirms are absent.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 29 terms including AI, AP-MS, breast cancer, Bridge2AI, cardiomyocyte, CM4AI, CRISPR/Cas9, iPSC, KOLF2.1J, MDA-MB-468, neural progenitor cell, paclitaxel, perturb-seq, protein-protein interaction, protein localization, scRNAseq, SEC-MS, subcellular imaging, vorinostat
sub_elements.quality_note: Well above the five-keyword threshold, spanning programme (Bridge2AI, CM4AI), biological material (two named cell lines and four cell types), assay methods (five), perturbagens (two named drugs) and analysis domain. Both expanded and abbreviated forms are given for several terms, which aids retrieval.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Terms are used correctly and are consistent with description and instances. 'mass spectroscopy' is a mild misnomer for mass spectrometry but is a common search variant and does not impair discovery. No clinical or patient terminology appears, which is consistent with the cell-line subject matter and is the evidence relied on for Element 4 applicability.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; file_collections enumerates five named sub-resources (immunofluorescence image archives, AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, release metadata) each with its own id, description, collection_type, file_count and compression
sub_elements.quality_note: The landing page is a well-formed persistent-id resolver URL on the hosting repository, and the release is decomposed into five described collections with sizes, giving a genuine hierarchical view of what the ten files are.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Landing page host matches the DOI registrant prefix. The five collection ids are fragments on the release DOI, which is a reasonable local naming scheme for sub-resources even though the fragments do not resolve independently.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven typed entries - four is_new_version_of (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM October 2025, doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R June 2025, doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX March 2025, doi:10.18130/V3/DXWOS5 initial release), two is_described_by (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311, doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734) and one references (doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3)
sub_elements.quality_note: The release is placed precisely in a quarterly lineage and tied to its describing literature, each link carrying a relationship type, a target DOI and a human-readable name. parent_datasets is not used, but the version lineage conveys the same hierarchy more informatively.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship types are used correctly: the prior quarterly releases are versions, the two preprints describe the data, and the Nature paper is a reference rather than a description, a distinction the record makes explicitly in a source_caveat because that study used U2OS cells rather than the lines in this release. The four version DOIs agree with version_access.versions_available.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms spells out CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with its attribution, non-commercial, ShareAlike and no-further-restrictions conditions and the commercial-negotiation route; license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; ip_restrictions.restrictions lists four items including 'Copyright to the datasets is held by the Regents of the University of California except where otherwise indicated' and 'Raw image data for spatial proteomics is copyright by The Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University'; data_governance.access_review_process states no access request is required for published files
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the licence and the intellectual-property position are stated concretely, including which institution holds copyright over which part of the release and who supervises commercial relicensing. The access route is unambiguous: public download, no application.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The IP allocation is consistent with data_collectors, which attributes the immunofluorescence imaging to the Lundberg Lab at Stanford and the mass-spectrometry work to UCSF. The record discloses that the copyright wording is transcribed from the March 2025 release because the June 2026 landing page does not restate it, which is a transparent provenance caveat rather than an unsupported assertion.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: unrestricted; regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions states the dataset does not involve human subjects, samples are de-identified and the data are not FDA regulated, and separately that clinical decision-making or patient-care use 'requires appropriate regulatory oversight and approval'; regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance cites FAIR Principles compliance as an NIH requirement and names Jillian Parker (jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu) as the Data Governance Committee contact
sub_elements.quality_note: A confidentiality classification is asserted from an enumerated vocabulary, the regulatory posture is stated across three specific axes (human subjects, de-identification, FDA), an applying use constraint is recorded, and a named governance contact with an email address is given, which is the governance-contact evidence the source rubric asks for.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: confidentiality_level: unrestricted is consistent with the public licence and with access_review_process requiring no application, and it is a semantically appropriate classification for cell-line laboratory data. hipaa_compliant is unstated, which is defensible since no PHI is claimed to be present. The clinical-use constraint is the E2 evidence that opens Element 4 sub-elements 1 and 2, and it is a constraint that applies rather than a record that none does.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats[0].access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; distribution_formats[1] describes 'Programmatic file access through the Dataverse data access API, recommended for archives above the web download size limit' with access_urls https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/; page gives the same landing page
sub_elements.quality_note: Scored on the 'platform access instructions' reading of this sub-element. The hosting platform is named, a resolvable landing page is supplied, and a second access route is given with an explicit reason for using it, which matters here because three archives are multi-gigabyte. A user can act on this.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The dedicated download_url slot is empty and the API base is a truncated endpoint that requires a datafile identifier the record never supplies for any of the ten archives, so the programmatic route is described rather than usable as printed. Recorded as a warning; the landing-page route is sufficient for the point.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats[0].format: 'ZIP archives containing RO-Crate packaged data files and metadata' with media_type: application/zip; file_collections each carry compression: zip with sizes (4.6 GB, 3.8 GB, 4.2 GB for the image archives; 113.3 KB and 135.8 KB for AP-MS; 171.8 KB and 93.9 KB for SEC-MS; 30.2 KB and 73.3 KB for perturb-seq; 1.1 MB for metadata); conforms_to names JSON-LD, RDF-XML and JSON-Schema serialisations
sub_elements.quality_note: A container format and a valid MIME type are stated explicitly, the packaging standard is named, and every archive carries a size so a user can plan a download. This is specific rather than boilerplate.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: application/zip is a correct IANA media type for the stated format. The payload formats inside the archives are not specified anywhere, so a user knows the container and the metadata serialisation but not how to parse the images or tables; recorded as a medium-severity issue and carried into Element 3 sub-element 2.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven typed entries with DOIs; external_resources: five groups covering two preprints with DOIs and a PMCID, four MassIVE deposits and a Figshare deposit, two embargoed perturb-seq links with a restrictions note, the CM4AI portal and data-releases page, and four tool links (github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io, fairscape.github.io, integrativemodeling.org)
sub_elements.quality_note: An unusually complete web of links: sibling releases, describing literature, the mirror deposits of the underlying raw data in MassIVE and Figshare, the project portal and the tooling documentation. The archival flag distinguishes durable deposits from project web pages.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The embargo status of the two perturb-seq external links is recorded rather than left as a dead link, with a source_caveat explaining that the June 2025 release listed SRA links and the June 2026 release supersedes them. This is consistent with known_limitations and third_party_sharing, both of which record the same embargo.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on E2 evidence: distribution_formats populated with access_urls, page resolves to a public Dataverse landing page, and the licence explicitly permits share and adapt.
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/. Users are free to share and adapt the material provided they give appropriate credit...'; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
sub_elements.quality_note: A named, versioned, standard open licence with a resolvable URL, its permissions and its three conditions written out, plus the attribution expectation and the route for uses the licence does not cover. A reuser can determine what they may do without consulting another document.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The licence name, the URL, the enumerated permission value and the prohibited_uses entries agree with one another. The non-commercial and ShareAlike restrictions are real limits on reuse but are clearly disclosed, which is what this sub-element asks for.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats, public landing page, reuse-permitting licence).
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats[0]: format 'ZIP archives containing RO-Crate packaged data files and metadata', media_type application/zip; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to states provenance is 'expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, serialized as JSON-LD and RDF-XML, with dataset schemas expressed in JSON-Schema'; file_collections carry compression: zip
sub_elements.quality_note: The formats that are named are genuinely standard and are exactly the ones that matter for machine consumption of the package: ZIP, RO-Crate, JSON-LD, RDF-XML, JSON-Schema. RO-Crate is itself an interoperability standard, and an RO-Crate carries per-file format declarations in its own metadata, so the packaging choice is substantive for reuse rather than nominal.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Character encoding is stated nowhere and the payload file formats are absent, so a reuser knows the container and metadata layer but not the parse format of the images or tables. Scored 1 because the named standards are specific, correct and actionable, with the payload gap recorded as a medium-severity issue.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats, public landing page, reuse-permitting licence).
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: 'RO-Crate (Research Object Crate)... each RO-Crate is assigned an ARK persistent identifier and carries an end-to-end provenance record expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, serialized as JSON-LD and RDF-XML, with dataset schemas expressed in JSON-Schema'; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset
sub_elements.quality_note: Four distinct conformance assertions at three levels: the packaging standard, the provenance ontology, the metadata schema of this datasheet itself with a resolvable w3id URI, and the class within it. This is among the strongest conformance statements the rubric contemplates.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The named standards are used correctly and coherently: RO-Crate as the package, EVI as the provenance vocabulary, JSON-LD/RDF-XML as serialisations of it, JSON-Schema for per-dataset schemas, and ARK as the within-crate identifier scheme. The conforms_to_schema URI is well-formed and matches the Bridge2AI data-sheets schema this record is written against.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats, public landing page, reuse-permitting licence), so the sub-element is scored rather than excluded.
sub_elements.evidence: No variables block anywhere in the record. instances describes four instance types in prose (image, SEC-MS elution profile, AP-MS measurement, single-cell transcriptome) with data_substrate and data_topic codes, but no variable identifiers, names, types, units or descriptions.
sub_elements.quality_note: Nothing in the record tells a reuser what the columns of the AP-MS, SEC-MS or perturb-seq tables are called, what they contain, or in what units. This is the single largest interoperability gap in an otherwise strongly interoperable record, and it bears directly on the element question about integrating this dataset with others.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The gap is consequential rather than formal: the release distributes quantitative tabular outputs whose reuse depends on column semantics, and the record supplies none. Scored 0 on the sub-element's own fields being absent with no substitute elsewhere.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)

Every named item falls into an excluded role: FAIRSCAPE performs packaging, provenance-metadata production and input validation, roles (c) and (d); the UVA Dataverse is hosting and serving, role (b); the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit is a capture reagent at acquisition, role (a); and node2vec, the HPA embedding model, the contrastive co-embedding, community detection, the Cell Mapping Toolkit and the Integrative Modeling Platform all belong to pipelines the record itself states produced outputs not in this release or that consume the release downstream, role (e). Naming the mass-spectrometry search software, the single-cell processing software and the image-handling software, with versions, would satisfy this sub-element.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: five typed entries - scope_limitation (interim release without predicted cell maps, with a recommended_mitigation pointing users to a later release or to the Cell Mapping Toolkit), coverage_limitation (the three modalities 'interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap', with a scope_impact noting analyses are limited to the intersection), temporal_limitation (pre-publication embargo on the perturb-seq external links), methodological_limitation ('Meaningful analysis of these data requires domain expertise') and a second coverage_limitation (imaging covers only MDA-MB-468; iPSC images forthcoming)
sub_elements.quality_note: Five limitations, each typed from a vocabulary, several carrying an explicit mitigation or a statement of analytical impact. These are real constraints that would change how a user plans an analysis, not defensive boilerplate.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Each limitation is corroborated elsewhere: the cell-map absence in missing_data_documentation and in the preprocessing caveats, the embargo in external_resources and third_party_sharing, the incomplete panel overlap in missing_data_patterns, and the expertise requirement in discouraged_uses. No limitation is asserted here and contradicted there.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: two entries with bias_type values from the enumerated taxonomy - representation_bias, described as data 'derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines [that] do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large', with affected_subsets naming both donor-derived lines and their donor demographics; and selection_bias, describing targeted rather than random selection of proteins and genes, with a mitigation_strategy citing the extension to a genome-scale screen of 11,739 genes; future_use_impacts: three entries including generalisation risk for models trained on these data and the Ethics module's governance framework
sub_elements.quality_note: Both entries use enumerated bias types, both explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the category, one carries a concrete mitigation, and the downstream social-impact dimension is covered in future_use_impacts.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Bias categorisation is semantically correct: two donor lines is genuinely a representation problem, and a targeted protein panel is genuinely a selection problem. The representation_bias wording matches sampling_strategies.why_not_representative verbatim and is consistent with is_representative: false, so the taxonomy label and the underlying sampling description agree.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: The anomalies field is absent. No other field documents anomalies in the data that are present: known_limitations addresses scope, coverage, embargo and required expertise; missing_data_documentation addresses what is absent; sampling_strategies addresses how the panels were chosen.
sub_elements.quality_note: Nothing tells a user what is wrong with the data they will download. For a release combining confocal imaging, two mass-spectrometry modalities and single-cell sequencing, the expected content is substantial: antibody specificity failures or excluded targets, image quality exclusions, failed or outlier mass-spectrometry runs, batch effects across conditions, and cell or guide filtering thresholds in the perturb-seq screens. None of it appears.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The one quality observation the record does make, that the June 2026 image archives share file sizes with the October 2025 archives but carry different MD5 checksums, is a packaging-integrity observation recorded in source_caveats for provenance reasons rather than an account of anomalies in the data content, and it is credited under Element 6 sub-element 3. The related claim in cleaning_strategies that acquisition-module data 'undergo quality control before release' asserts that quality control happened without reporting what it found.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements[0].sensitive_elements_present: false, with sensitivity_details: 'The release records no human subjects and de-identified samples; the released content consists of laboratory measurements on commercially available human cell lines (immunofluorescence images, mass spectrometry-derived interaction data and single-cell sequencing summaries) rather than personal identifiers or protected health information.'
sub_elements.quality_note: An explicit negative determination accompanied by a reason: the record states what the content actually is and why that content is not sensitive, rather than leaving an empty field or an unexplained false. Per the instrument, an explicit false flag with reasoning is meaningful documentation.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistent with is_deidentified, with human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false and with confidentiality_level: unrestricted. content_warnings is absent, which is appropriate where no sensitive content is identified. The determination is plausible for the data types named, subject to the genotype-linkage caveat recorded under Element 4 sub-element 2.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review and Social Impact Analysis
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews[0] describes the CM4AI Ethics module's Value-Sensitive Design methodology, 'an axiological repository of values, and a CM4AI Life Cycle framework elucidating governance milestones throughout data generation and AI system development', plus mixed qualitative and quantitative empirical research to capture community insights, with reviewing_organization and contact_person; future_use_impacts: three entries covering non-generalisation of models trained on two cell lines, the Ethics module's integration of anticipated applications into governance frameworks 'to optimize benefits, mitigate potential risks and promote use for the collective good', and clinical or patient-care application without regulatory oversight as an identified foreseeable misuse
sub_elements.quality_note: Both halves of the sub-element are substantive. The social-impact analysis is not generic: it names a specific foreseeable misuse, a specific generalisation risk tied to the dataset's own composition, and a governance apparatus with named deliverables.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The foreseeable-misuse statement in future_use_impacts is consistent with the matching prohibited_uses entry and with the clinical-oversight constraint in regulatory_restrictions, three fields agreeing on the same risk. The generalisation impact is consistent with known_biases representation_bias. Conflicts of interest are not addressed, a minor gap within the sub-element's scope.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on E2 evidence (distribution_formats populated, public Dataverse landing page, reuse-permitting licence).
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; citation ends 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; description states the data 'are archived in the University of Virginia Dataverse'; maintainers names 'University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), School of Medicine collection'; retention_limit commits to 'Long term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse'; the DOI prefix 10.18130 is the UVA Dataverse registrant
sub_elements.quality_note: The hosting platform is a recognised institutional Dataverse repository and is identified unambiguously by five independent fields plus the DOI prefix, together with an explicit long-term preservation commitment backed by institutional funds.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The dedicated publisher slot is empty, and source_caveats justifies this on the ground that 'The bundle names no publisher for the release', which sits awkwardly against the record's own citation naming the UVA Dataverse in the publisher position; recorded as a medium-severity consistency issue. Scored 1 because the platform is identified beyond doubt by the fields the sub-element asks a reader to consult. Separately, notes discloses that the hosting collection 'is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives', an availability risk worth reading alongside the preservation commitment.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met; per #1080 this sub-element is scored whenever that condition holds, without requiring an existing publication.
sub_elements.evidence: citation: a complete formatted data citation listing all 47 authors, the year 2026, the title in quotation marks, 'https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; license_and_use_terms.notes adds that 'community norms and good scientific practices expect proper credit to be given via citation, using the data citation shown on the dataset page' and that publications should cite both the related publication and the data collection directly
sub_elements.quality_note: A ready-to-use citation string in repository-standard form, a resolvable DOI, and explicit citation instructions covering the dual obligation to cite both the data and the describing paper. This is the complete set the rubric's note for Bridge2AI datasets calls for.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The citation's DOI, repository and version agree with the doi, page and version fields. The DOI resolves under a registrant prefix consistent with the named repository.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats, public landing page, reuse-permitting licence).
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to names RO-Crate with ARK persistent identifiers, the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, JSON-LD and RDF-XML serialisations and JSON-Schema dataset schemas; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance cites compliance with the FAIR Principles for data and software as an NIH requirement
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is asserted against five recognised community standards spanning packaging, provenance, serialisation, schema and identifier practice, plus the FAIR Principles. Each is named specifically enough to be checked.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The standards named are real, current and used in the roles they actually serve; the combination of RO-Crate packaging with an EVI provenance graph in JSON-LD is coherent rather than a list of buzzwords. The w3id conforms_to_schema URI is well-formed and identifies the schema this record is written against.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats, public landing page, reuse-permitting licence).
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: 'CM4AI project portal, including documentation, data releases, tools and training: https://cm4ai.org/', 'CM4AI data releases page: https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/', 'Cell Mapping Toolkit user documentation: https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/', 'FAIRSCAPE AI-readiness framework, with tutorial and installation instructions: https://fairscape.github.io', 'Integrative Modeling Platform (IMP) package: http://integrativemodeling.org'; page gives the dataset landing page; maintainers gives a programme-management contact (snthaker@uab.edu) for project inquiries
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation is linked at three levels: the project portal with training material, the tooling user documentation on readthedocs, and the framework tutorial and installation instructions, alongside the dataset landing page and a named human contact for inquiries.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All URLs are well-formed with plausible domains, and the archival: false flag correctly marks these as project web resources rather than durable deposits. The distinction between archival and non-archival external resources is applied consistently across the five groups.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats, public landing page, reuse-permitting licence).
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven entries, each with relationship_type, target_dataset DOI and name - is_new_version_of for doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX and doi:10.18130/V3/DXWOS5; is_described_by for doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 and doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734; references for doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3
sub_elements.quality_note: Every relationship is typed from a recognisable vocabulary and resolves to a DOI with a human-readable name. Three distinct relationship semantics are used, and each is the right one for its target.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The typing is semantically careful. The Nature paper is typed references rather than is_described_by, and a source_caveat explains why: it 'reports a multimodal cell map of U2OS osteosarcoma cells ... it is a separate study rather than a description of the cell lines and conditions in this release'. The fourth is_new_version_of target carries a caveat declining to equate it with the portal's undated 'May 2024 Data Release' because no source makes that association. This is exactly the discrimination the sub-element rewards.

strengths: Identifier and provenance discipline across the whole record: a Dataverse DOI whose prefix, landing-page host and citation all agree, cell-line RRIDs, ORCIDs for 38 of 47 creators, ROR affiliations, four correctly formed NIH award numbers with application number, awardee, PI and project period, and a version lineage of five DOIs that agrees between related_datasets and version_access.

Exceptional source transparency. A record-level source_caveats and eleven field-level caveats name each source conflict, state which source was preferred and why, and decline to assert figures the sources do not support - including the striking observation that the June 2026 image archives share file sizes with the October 2025 archives but carry different MD5 checksums, from which the record infers regeneration and refuses to carry over the earlier protein counts.

Standards conformance is asserted at five levels and coherently: RO-Crate packaging with ARK identifiers, EVI Evidence Graph Ontology provenance, JSON-LD and RDF-XML serialisation, JSON-Schema dataset schemas and the Bridge2AI data-sheets schema itself, backed by a FAIR compliance statement.

The limitations, bias and missing-data fields form a consistent and genuinely useful account: five typed limitations with mitigations and scope impacts, two enumerated bias types with mechanisms and a concrete mitigation, and a missing-data block that names each absence, attributes a cause and states a handling strategy - all agreeing with one another and with discouraged_uses.

Ethical governance is documented appropriately for a dataset with no human participants: a named ethics body with a described methodology, three contactable individuals with email addresses across governance and ethics-review roles, a reasoned account of why no IRB approval exists, and explicit false flags for human subjects and sensitive elements that carry justifications rather than standing bare.

Collection methodology is described at methods-section depth, naming reagent sources, automation, confocal channel counts, guide multiplicity, the inducible dCas9 system, the specific commercial readout kit and which of four institutions performed each modality.
weaknesses: The processing documentation does not describe the released data. Six source_caveats state that the preprocessing, labeling and first cleaning entries belong to the MuSIC pipeline whose cell maps are not in this release, one saying outright that the step 'was not applied to the artifacts distributed here'. Three of five file_collections are typed processed_data, yet no search, quantification, alignment, filtering or image-processing step is described for them.

No software is named that produced or transformed the distributed files. What is named is packaging and provenance software (FAIRSCAPE), a hosting platform (Dataverse), a capture reagent (the 10x 3'HT kit) and downstream or out-of-release pipelines (node2vec, the HPA embedding model, the Cell Mapping Toolkit, IMP). No version number appears for any of them, and no used_software is attached to any property.

Variable-level metadata is entirely absent: no variables block, no is_tabular flag, no data dictionary. The release distributes quantitative tables whose columns are undocumented, which blocks the integration this record otherwise prepares for so thoroughly.

No anomalies documentation. Nothing records antibody failures, image exclusions, failed or outlier mass-spectrometry runs, batch effects, or cell and guide filtering thresholds, and the one quality-control statement that does apply to the release reports that QC happened without reporting what it found.

Format description stops at the container. ZIP and RO-Crate with a correct MIME type are given, but the payload formats inside the archives and the character encoding of text files are unstated, so a user knows how to unpack the release but not how to parse it.

Release-scope instance counts are largely unstated, a consequence of the record's own scope discipline: the portal figures are correctly flagged as cumulative across releases and the earlier protein counts are correctly not carried over, leaving 11,739 targeted genes as the only release-scope sample count.

Two slots are empty against the record's own evidence: publisher is omitted on the ground that no source names one, while the record's citation names the University of Virginia Dataverse in the publisher position; and download_url is empty, with the programmatic access route given as an API base that needs file identifiers the record never supplies.
recommendations: Add preprocessing_strategies and cleaning_strategies entries for the pipeline that actually produced the released AP-MS, SEC-MS and perturb-seq archives, and attach used_software with versions to each - the mass-spectrometry search and quantification software, the single-cell alignment and counting software, and the image-handling software - keeping the MuSIC steps clearly labelled as downstream methodology.

Add a variables block with identifiers, types, units and descriptions for the columns of each tabular collection, and set is_tabular on those collections, so the release can be integrated rather than only downloaded.
Add per-collection format and media_type entries for the archive contents and state the character encoding of text files, so the RO-Crate packaging claim is matched by payload-level parseability.

Add an anomalies block covering known quality issues in the released imaging, mass-spectrometry and single-cell data, including the filtering already applied and the residual artifacts users should expect, and report what the acquisition-module quality control found rather than only that it occurred.

Populate publisher with University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData) and download_url with the resolvable access URL, and list the Dataverse file identifiers so the documented API route becomes usable.

Report release-scope counts per modality (images per condition, cells per perturb-seq archive, baits and interactions per AP-MS archive), or state explicitly that the sources do not provide them, preserving the record's scope discipline while closing the gap.

Strengthen the de-identification entry with a short residual-risk note addressing genotype-based linkage from the released sequence-derived data, and add an imputation_protocols entry stating the imputation method used for missing quantitative values or that none was applied.

Record the award numbers in a grant-identifier slot rather than as non-resolvable DOI fragments, and note in retention_limit that the hosting collection is under review, so the preservation commitment is read alongside the disclosed risk.
